deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a fair copy of a systematic treatment of the genus-3 (plane quartic) case. The previous page is signed 'H.W.', so it is most likely Heinrich Weber's working-up of Riemann's theory. The curve is written as sqrt(x*xi)+sqrt(y*eta)+sqrt(z*zeta)=0 (eq. 9). Here x,y,z,xi,eta,zeta are six of the 28 'Abel'sche Functionen' (square roots of bitangent linear forms). They satisfy three linear relations, normalised in (16) as
  x+y+z+xi+eta+zeta=0,
  a x+b y+c z+xi/a+eta/b+zeta/c=0 (a,b,c = alpha,beta,gamma),
  a'x+b'y+c'z+xi/a'+eta/b'+zeta/c'=0.
A fourth relation of the same shape (17), with unknown a'',b'',c'', must follow from these. Writing it as a combination with multipliers lambda, lambda', lambda'' gives (18): lambda''a'' = lambda a + lambda'a' + 1 and lambda''/a'' = lambda/a + lambda'/a' + 1, and likewise for b, c. Multiplying each pair gives (19): lambda''^2 = lambda^2 + lambda'^2 + 1 + lambda lambda'(a/a'+a'/a) + lambda(a+1/a) + lambda'(a'+1/a'), and analogously for b, c. All of this is on the previous page.

This page, step 1 (my reconstruction of the implicit step). Subtract the b-equation of (19) from the a-equation, and the c-equation from the a-equation. Then divide by lambda*lambda'. This gives two linear equations in 1/lambda, 1/lambda':
  0 = (1/lambda')(a+1/a-b-1/b) + (1/lambda)(a'+1/a'-b'-1/b') + (a/a'+a'/a-b/b'-b'/b),
and the same with c in place of b.
Geometrically, (c0:c1:c2)=(1:lambda:lambda') are the coordinates of the combination in the net spanned by the three relations. The two conditions Q_a=Q_b=Q_c are two conics through the three coordinate vertices, which correspond to the three given relations. The fourth intersection point is unique, and the equations are linear in the reciprocals. So lambda and lambda' are determined uniquely ('eindeutig').

Step 2. One equation of (19) gives lambda'' up to sign. Then (18) gives a'', b'', c'' up to a common sign. That sign is inherently undetermined, since (17) multiplied by -1 is the same relation with (a'',b'',c'') replaced by -(a'',b'',c'').

Footnote *. Abbreviate (a,b,c) = det[[1,1,1],[a,b,c],[a',b',c']], and (1/a,b,c) etc. for the same determinant with a,a' replaced by 1/a,1/a'. Then a'',b'',c'' can be read off directly from products of these determinants: one equation for a a' a''·b b' b'' and one for a a' a'' : b b' b'', plus the analogous ones. The exact arrangement of the determinant factors is partly illegible; see the corrections below.

Step 3. With the four relations (index 0,1,2,3, coefficients 1; a,b,c; a',b',c'; a'',b'',c''), the next page shows how each relation produces pairs of bitangents. If a x+b y+c z+xi/a+eta/b+zeta/c=0, then p=a x+b y+c z and q=xi/a+eta/b+c z satisfy (my verification):
  p q = (a x+b y)(xi/a+eta/b) - z zeta = (sqrt(a/b) sqrt(x eta) - sqrt(b/a) sqrt(y xi))^2,
using z zeta = (sqrt(x xi)+sqrt(y eta))^2. So sqrt(p) sqrt(q) lies in the group (Riemann's 'Gruppe', i.e. a fixed sum of characteristics) of sqrt(x eta), sqrt(y xi). The page accordingly lists:
- group sqrt(x eta), sqrt(y xi): the four pairs sqrt(a x+b y+c z), sqrt(xi/a+eta/b+c z) for the four coefficient systems;
- group sqrt(x zeta), sqrt(z xi): sqrt(a x+b y+c z), sqrt(xi/a+b y+zeta/c);
- group sqrt(y zeta), sqrt(z eta): sqrt(a x+b y+c z), sqrt(a x+eta/b+zeta/c).
The four functions sqrt(a x+b y+c z) are common to all three groups. That gives 4 + 3*4 = 16 new bitangents beyond the 6 given, i.e. 22 of the 28.

Step 4 (characteristics). The three groups share four functions, so the corresponding groups of characteristics share four characteristics. These are assigned arbitrarily to sqrt(x+y+z), sqrt(a x+...), sqrt(a'x+...), sqrt(a''x+...). Everything else is then forced by the pairing structure. Notation: (p),(q),(r) are the group characteristics of sqrt(y zeta), sqrt(z xi), sqrt(x eta); (d),(e),(f),(g) are those of the four common functions; (n+p) is that of sqrt(x). The resulting table, (20), appears on the previous page: e.g. (sqrt(x+eta+zeta)) = (p+d), (sqrt(xi/a+eta/b+c z)) = (r+e), etc.
errors: As transcribed, the elimination equations put 1/lambda with (a+1/a-b-1/b) and 1/lambda' with (a'+1/a'-b'-1/b'). The correct result of subtracting the (19) equations and dividing by lambda*lambda' pairs 1/lambda' with (a+1/a-b-1/b) and 1/lambda with (a'+1/a'-b'-1/b'). Either the manuscript has a prime slip or the transcription dropped a prime; the image suggests the first factor may indeed be 1/lambda'.

The footnote's determinant formulas as transcribed fail the symmetry test. Under a,a',a''->1/a,1/a',1/a'' (swapping x and xi), the transcribed first equation does not transform consistently. A consistent form is: a a' a''·b b' b'' = (a,b,c)(a,b,1/c) : (1/a,1/b,c)(1/a,1/b,1/c), and a a' a'' : b b' b'' = (a,1/b,c)(a,1/b,1/c) : (1/a,b,c)(1/a,b,1/c). This is probably what is written, but I have not verified it.
No mathematical error in the main text. The statement that the common sign of a'',b'',c'' remains undetermined is correct and harmless, since the relation (17) is invariant under it.

results.what: Determination of the fourth linear relation of type a x+b y+c z+xi/a+eta/b+zeta/c=0 from three given ones. It reduces to the fourth intersection point of two conics through three known points, which yields linear equations in 1/lambda, 1/lambda'.
results.modern_name: Construction of the remaining bitangents of a plane quartic from a given configuration; fourth base point of a pencil of conics via the Cremona (reciprocal) transformation
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann's genus-3 theory, as worked out by H. Weber ('Zur Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen für den Fall p=3', Riemann's Werke 1876; Weber, Theorie der Abelschen Functionen vom Geschlecht 3, 1876)

results.what: Closed-form expressions for a'',b'',c'' as ratios of products of 3x3 determinants built from a,a',b,b',c,c' and their reciprocals (footnote)
results.modern_name: Explicit parametrization of the bitangent coefficients
results.usually_credited_to: Weber's elaboration of Riemann's p=3 theory

results.what: Production of 16 further bitangents (4 common plus 3 groups of 4 pairs) from the 6 given, with the identity p q = (sqrt(a/b) sqrt(x eta) - sqrt(b/a) sqrt(y xi))^2 placing the pairs in the groups sqrt(x eta),sqrt(y xi) etc.
results.modern_name: 28 bitangents of a plane quartic and their organization by theta characteristics (Steiner complexes / syzygetic groups)
results.usually_credited_to: Steiner, Hesse (1855), Aronhold (1864); in theta-characteristic form Riemann/Weber (1876)

results.what: Assignment of characteristics to the 16 new bitangents from the pairing structure: arbitrary choice of the 4 common characteristics, the rest forced
results.modern_name: Correspondence between bitangents and odd theta characteristics in genus 3

deep.surprise_reason: This is a fair copy (apparently by H. Weber, initials on the preceding page) of material that appears essentially as published in 'Zur Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen für den Fall p=3' in Riemann's Werke (1876) and in Weber's 1876 monograph. The algebra is routine and the results are already attributed to Riemann/Weber.

transcription_corrections: 'Eliminirt man nun auf zu zweien derselben' should read 'Eliminirt man nun aus je zweien derselben λ''' (eliminating λ'' from pairs of the equations (19)).
The first elimination term is likely 1/λ'(α+1/α-β-1/β) and the second 1/λ(α'+1/α'-β'-1/β'), not as transcribed.
'in der Gruppe √(xξ),√(yη)' should read 'in der Gruppe √(xη), √(yξ)'; this is mathematically required, since sqrt(p q) is a combination of sqrt(x eta) and sqrt(y xi).
'in der Gruppe √(xξ),√(zζ)' should read 'in der Gruppe √(xζ), √(zξ)'.
'in der Gruppe √(yη),√(zζ)' should read 'in der Gruppe √(yζ), √(zη)'.
'(u+p)' should read '(n+p)', the characteristic of √x, consistent with the previous page.
Footnote denominators/numerators: likely (α,β,γ)(α,β,1/γ) : (1/α,1/β,γ)(1/α,1/β,1/γ) for the product, and (α,1/β,γ)(α,1/β,1/γ) : (1/α,β,γ)(1/α,β,1/γ) for the quotient.
'(Unten unter dem Texte[?])' is the editorial note 'Unten unter den Text' (place footnote at bottom); the struck word after the footnote is a deleted initial or abbreviation.
'Auf der gleichen Weise' should read 'Auf die gleiche Weise'.
